name_es: Juan Andrés («el Moro Alfaquí», Joan Andreu)
name_orig: Juan Andrés, quondam alfaquí (Spanish; Latin Joannes Andreas)
born: c. 1460s–1480s (per Wikipedia: before 1475; baptised 1487 per team brief)
role_place: Former Muslim jurist (alfaquí) from Xàtiva, convert and priest; author of the 1515 Valencia polemic.
why_relevant: Author of the 1515 Confusión o confutación, which states that Muhammad married Aixa/Axa at six and consummated it at eight, with an explicit reproach.
fame: Known mainly through his 1515 book, which was widely reprinted and translated (Italian 1537, French 1574, English 1652). Scholars debate whether he is a historical person (Wiegers); a canon named Juan Andrés appears in Granada records c. 1516 (per a search snippet, not read).
community: Converted Muslim turned Catholic priest (Latin Catholic)
